cve_summary: The translate_desc function in drivers/vhost/vhost.c in the Linux kernel before 3.7 does not properly handle cross-region descriptors, which allows guest OS users to obtain host OS privileges by leveraging KVM guest OS privileges.
commit_message:
vhost: fix length for cross region descriptor

If a single descriptor crosses a region, the
second chunk length should be decremented
by size translated so far, instead it includes
the full descriptor length.

Signed-off-by: Michael S. Tsirkin <mst@redhat.com>
Acked-by: Jason Wang <jasowang@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Translates a memory address range into an array of I/O vector structures.

Parameters: 
dev (struct vhost_dev *): Pointer to the vhost device structure.
addr (u64): The starting address to translate.
len (u32): The length of the address range to translate.
iov (struct iovec[]): Array of I/O vector structures to be filled.
iov_size (int): The size of the I/O vector array.

Returns: 
int: The number of I/O vectors filled, or a negative error code on failure.

Logic: 
The function locks the read access to the device's memory, iterates over the specified address range, and populates the provided I/O vector array with the corresponding user-space addresses and lengths. It checks for buffer overflows and invalid memory regions, returning appropriate error codes if encountered. Finally, it unlocks the read access and returns the count of filled I/O vectors.
"""
